LibraryOriginal edition

Paper Retrieval

A useful collection connects a question to work worth reading and to the actual text behind its citation. Relevance, bibliographic coverage, access, and file identity are different claims. Keep each visible so the reader can trust the result without repeating the search. This portable package requires a search or HTTP/browser capability supplied by the recipient host; it does not install an authenticated browser or grant library access. Use the companion research for evidence selection, current external investigation and conflicting-source assessment; this Skill owns scholarly identity, acquisition and text verification. See setup and dependencies and the sources and verification guide.

For controlled or authenticated pages, retain a separate browser/session owner using browser-relay for exact target custody, authorized session reuse, destination/readback verification, desktop placement and cleanup. A browser API is the execution capability; a companion Skill supplies its method and ownership contract. Neither provides entitlement. The dependency table distinguishes companion methods from host capabilities. For evidenced network faults, use network with the recipient’s configured diagnosis capabilities; a retrieval failure does not itself authorize proxy, DNS or routing changes.

Establish the collection

Resolve question, authors, languages, date range, selected versus exhaustive scope, requested editions/versions, and destination from the task. Inspect an existing manifest before downloading. Select substantive relevant contributions by abstract and, where available, argument, conclusion and references. Explain their contribution; prestige and citation counts alone do not establish quality. Mark abstract-only relevance judgments as provisional.

For an author bibliography, verify identity through official CV/faculty pages, coauthors, field, title and affiliation history. Names and transliterations alone are insufficient. Keep current institutional grouping distinct from affiliation printed on an older work. Separate verified bibliographic coverage from obtained texts. For books resolve author/editor, language/translation, publisher, edition and ISBN; for chapters identify the containing book as well.

Discover and reconcile

Search exact titles and meaningful variants, official author pages, publishers, DOI records and disciplinary/university repositories. Scholar's versions view, Crossref/OpenAlex, repository indexes and open-location services supply different evidence. Follow records to their original source. A closed-access flag or failed profile search does not establish that no author copy exists.

For Chinese works, combine author bibliographies, journal/university sites and Chinese indexes such as CNKI or NSSD when available. Inspect actual result rows, including asynchronous results; a heading/count is not a verified bibliography. Cross-check conflicting metadata against publisher records and the text. Preserve the source citation and explain supported corrections. Article, chapter, book and review-container identifiers are not interchangeable. Record search sources and remaining coverage rather than claiming exhaustive absence from a single index.

Acquire available text

Use a labelled direct public file or the repository/publisher's official download control. For a public HTTPS PDF, a concrete CLI route is:

curl --fail --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --output candidate.pdf 'DIRECT_PDF_URL'
python3 scripts/inspect_pdf.py candidate.pdf

Replace the placeholder with an inspected public file URL. curl does not handle interactive login, CAPTCHA, institutional access or JavaScript download controls. For those, use the host's available browser/download API within the task's actual authorization, or download through the recipient's normal authorized interface and inspect the local file. Associate the returned file with the initiating work and download action. Reconcile an uncertain prior download before retrying. Reuse a session only under its owner's actual authorization. Separate owned pages may share a session; extra browser instances do not establish throughput or entitlement. Page-local response capture can be associated with its initiating page. If a browser-wide download channel is shared, serialize capture or use a supported unique initiating-action identifier and verify its matching completion; otherwise concurrent downloads cannot be safely attributed. Preserve the official navigation/control path when source validation depends on it. Distinguish transport, visible challenge, session, entitlement, format and capture failure. Do not export cookies, derive entitlement from a logged-in page, evade site restrictions, or use private adapters. Preserve existing personal authentication, consent, payment and outbound-contact boundaries; reuse authorization already given. A technical failure alone is not proof of denied entitlement.

Verify before adoption

Run the bundled inspector for PDF signature, parseability, page count, SHA-256, and first/last-page text. These checks deliberately report identity/completeness as unverified. Inspect title, authors, year, publication/version information, body coverage, ending and references against the intended record. Render pages with pdftoppm or a PDF viewer when text is absent or unclear. Inspect intervening pages/contents when the scope requires it; endpoints alone cannot detect missing middle pages. HTTP success, filenames and %PDF- do not prove the correct work. Reject HTML/errors, wrong works, previews and damaged files. Compare hashes across the collection to detect repeated bytes returned under different citations.

Identify format by bytes even when extension is .caj. Preserve a genuine CAJ/KDH original if obtained; conversion needs a separately available legitimate tool. Verify any derivative independently. Do not reconstruct a purported original from webpage text. Label manuscripts, preprints, translations, OCR, excerpts, appended abstract sheets and composition differences accurately; none silently becomes the version of record or a complete book.

Keep original files and an existing manifest schema. A new small manifest needs title, authors, year/edition, verified identifiers and stable source links, local file, version, retrieval date, hash, identity/completeness evidence, and relevant limits. Store neither signed download URLs nor session secrets. Deduplicate by identifier, edition/version and bytes; retain materially different versions. Respect the destination's link/rename conventions when reorganizing.

Resolve and report gaps

For every selected work without the requested verified text, record the actual condition: unresolved identity, unconfirmed version, unsearched source coverage, technical failure, personal authentication step, confirmed entitlement limit, or no open copy exposed by the inspected sources. These conditions can coexist; not_found alone is insufficient. Continue recoverable work and independent accessible items. Seek another fitting source, meaningful title variants or format route when evidence supports it. Stop an item only at an evidenced external boundary or the user's stopping scope, with a concrete resume condition.

Keep observed dates, attempted route/result, remaining coverage, next action, and whether personal participation is useful in the owning manifest. Notify the user when the actual next action requires their participation, rather than asking them to repair technical failures. At the handoff, identify every still required incomplete work directly in the conversation: title, author, year or edition, missing scope, supported stable link and copyable verified DOI/ISBN or other source-labelled identifier. Distinguish partial/unverified files, obtained alternate versions, and optional upgrades. A count or manifest link cannot replace that per-item explanation. Acquired text and remaining gaps are separate results; inaccessible scholarship is not absent scholarship.
